title: Gravitation: From Falling Apples to Orbiting Satellites

questions.question: Kepler's third law of planetary motion states that:
questions.rationale: The square of a planet's period is proportional to the cube of its semi-major axis: T² ∝ a³.

questions.question: What is the value of the universal gravitational constant G?
questions.rationale: G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg², the same everywhere in the universe; 9.8 is Earth's surface g, not G.

questions.question: Henry Cavendish's 1798 torsion-balance experiment is famous for:
options: First measuring G, thereby 'weighing the Earth'
questions.rationale: Cavendish measured G in the laboratory; substituting it into g = GM/R² gave Earth's mass (about 6 × 10²⁴ kg) for the first time.

questions.question: As altitude above the Earth increases, the acceleration due to gravity:
options: Becomes zero just above the surface
questions.rationale: g = GM/R² falls off with distance: it drops from 9.8 m/s² to about 8.7 m/s² at the ISS's 400 km height.

questions.question: Which quantity changes when an astronaut travels from Earth to the Moon?
questions.rationale: Mass (kg) never changes with location, but weight W = mg does: the lesson's 60 kg student weighs 588 N on Earth and about 97 N on the Moon.

questions.question: The escape velocity from the Earth's surface is approximately:
questions.rationale: vₑ = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s for Earth; 7.9 km/s is the near-surface orbital velocity, which is smaller.

questions.question: A geostationary satellite has which combination of properties?
options: 24-hour period, about 36,000 km high, orbiting west to east above the equator
100-minute period, 800 km high, crossing the poles
12-hour period, 20,000 km high, above the equator
Fixed on the ground with a 24-hour period
questions.rationale: Geostationary satellites match Earth's 24-hour spin at ~36,000 km above the equator, so they appear fixed in the sky.

questions.question: Mapping, spying, and crop and forest monitoring are typical uses of which satellites?
questions.rationale: Polar satellites at 700–800 km cross every latitude every ~100 minutes, making them ideal for mapping and monitoring.

questions.question: Spring tides (the strongest tides) occur when:
options: The Moon is at half phase
Sun and Moon line up at new and full moon
The Earth is farthest from the Sun
questions.rationale: At new and full moon the solar and lunar pulls add together to give spring tides; at half moon they partially cancel, giving neap tides.

questions.question: Using Kepler's third law with a = 1.52 AU for Mars, the orbital period is about:
questions.rationale: T = √(a³) = √(1.52³) ≈ 1.88 years, the value the lesson's info box confirms by observation.
